readme.excerpt: English 简体中文 繁體中文 한국어 Español 日本語 हिन्दी मराठी Русский Português తెలుగు Français Deutsch Italiano Tiếng Việt العربية اردو বাংলা فارسی Română Türkçe State-of-the-art pretrained models for inference and training Transformers is the model-definition framework for machine learning models in text, computer vision, audio, video, and multimodal tasks. It defines each model once, in PyTorch, and you use that definition for both inference and training. Training frameworks, inference engines, and local runtimes build on that definition instead of writing their own. Transformers adds new architectures as they're released and matches each one to its original results, so those tools get each new model as soon as it's added. Fine-tune with less memory. Unsloth trains LLMs in 4-bit, 8-bit, and 16-bit precision with custom kernels. Serve LLMs at scale. vLLM batches requests continuously and keeps KV cache memory compact with PagedAttention. Serve LLMs with low latency. SGLang is a high-throughput inference engine with a frontend language for agentic workflows. Run LLMs locally without Python. llama.cpp is a C/C++ inference engine that runs quantized models in the GGUF format. Transformers standardizes how every model is written, so hundreds of architectures share one structure.
